From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP: Pegasus Health — technical trial metrics & owners

Alex,

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation and helpful context on your expected traffic patterns and PHI handling. Per our call I drafted a short Mutual Action Plan milestone focused on the technical evaluation so we have alignment on owners, success criteria, and blockers. Attaching the draft MAP and the latency benchmark template.

High-level milestones (draft):
- Milestone 1 — Trial kickoff and environment provisioning
  * Owner: Ben Carter (SE)
  * Target date: 2027-03-24 (kickoff meeting + temporary trial creds)
  * Dependencies: Pegasus provides 2k de-identified sample queries, list of priority intents, HIPAA evidentiary items for logging

- Milestone 2 — Performance & latency benchmarks (initial run)
  * Owner: Ben Carter
  * Success criteria: P95 latency <= 300ms for typical 128-token requests; sustained throughput 20 rps with 80ms jitter; token cost <= $0.003/token (config-dependent)
  * Target date: 2027-03-31
  * Attachments: latency-benchmark-template.csv

- Milestone 3 — Quality validation (functional)
  * Owner: Pegasus / joint evaluation
  * Success criteria: entity extraction F1 >= 0.78 on sample set; zero critical privacy violations on sampled outputs
  * Target date: 2027-04-07

- Milestone 4 — Model shortlisting and fallback policy
  * Owner: Redwood (Ben) + Pegasus (Alex)
  * Candidate models: Llama-3-13B-q4f, Falcon-40B-ctr, OpenRedwood-2-70B (quantized variants for cost)
  * Fallback: smaller quantized variant with automatic routing if latency SLO missed

Open questions / blockers I noted during the call:
- HIPAA logging requirements and any additional audit artifacts required for the trial environment
- Can Pegasus provide the 2k sample queries de-identified by COB 2027-03-23?
- Any hard cost ceiling we should use for the trial (we proposed $0.003/token as a working target)

Next steps:
1) I will upload the MAP draft to the shared Drive and attach here (pegasus_map_draft_v1.pdf).
2) Ben will provision a trial config and run initial latency tests after we receive the sample data.
3) Alex — confirm HIPAA logging bullets and preferred kickoff time on 3/24.

Thanks — short and actionable. If that looks right I will formalize dates and add to the HubSpot deal.

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Putting some technical clarity against the proposed success criteria so we have a reproducible runbook: 

- Test corpus: 2,000 de-identified queries (mix: 60% short tickets <=32 tokens, 30% medium 32-128, 10% long 128-512)
- Evaluation harness: 3 warm-up runs, then 5 measured runs across a 2-minute sustained window to capture throughput behavior
- Batch sizes: target single-request latency but we will test batching=1,4,8 to show cost/latency tradeoffs
- Metrics to record: P50/P95/P99 latency (ms), 95th-percentile GPU mem, tokens/generated, token-cost estimate, quality F1 per intent
- Failure modes: throttling backoff behavior, KV-cache hit-rate (if enabled), and model fallbacks

I can own the latency runs and will publish the CSV from latency-benchmark-template.csv to the shared Drive. Two asks for Pegasus: 1) SFTP or signed URL for sample set; 2) confirm whether we can run the trial in a pseudo-prod region in us-west-2 (we will mirror your region for network parity).

I expect to have initial results and a short slide with charts by 2027-03-31.

--
